kind: Two pilots at full size, one seed each, 24,000 updates: skip fibres on the lifted loop with power-law cells, and the same loop at twice the rate, each beside the lifted loop with power-law cells. They run on GPU 1 in the hours it has left in the window of 2026-11-26/27, after fsp-lift and pool_gradient's jobs.
why: The lifted loop with power-law cells is fsp-lift2's recipe and the best pilot at full size (fs-loop6-lift-pw8 1.287005, full_size_power_cells.json): 0.0033 behind the rate pilot's Transformer at the same rate (1.28370) and 0.0108 behind it at its best rate (1.27625). Two changes that need no new code had steady gains that fell under their own marks. Skip fibres on the looped bed led by 0.0066 and 0.0062 on both server seeds after 24,000 updates, intervals clear of zero (skip_fibres_with_data.json, result_server_looped: under that record's 0.010 mark, so a fail), at the laptop's seed mostly on far copies, where power-law cells gain least. The lifted loop at 1.2e-3 was 0.0031 better than at 6e-4, interval clear of zero (full_size_loop_variants.json, result_rate: under the 0.005 mark, so the rate stayed 6e-4); power-law cells learn faster early on the bed (power_cells_screen.json), so their best rate may differ from plain cells'. Each pilot is a cheap check of what the weekend's next full-length run should carry. Neither can change fsp-lift2, which starts the same evening with its recipe fixed (full_size_lifted_loop_second.json).

arms.fs-loop6-lift-pw8-skip: sched/bin/full.sh stack fs-loop6-lift-pw8-skip --lr 6e-4 --stack-loop 2,8,2 --pulse-budget 507000 --pool-lifts-ceiling --granule-power 8 --stack-skips level, on the code copy of f876392 (v18c): 34,976,788 parameters, 0.48% more than fs-loop6-lift-pw8 (34,810,900) and 0.65% more than the Transformer's 34,752,000; the skip fibres' gains are the only new parameters, and every pass of the loop has its own
arms.fs-loop12-lift-pw8: sched/bin/full.sh stack fs-loop12-lift-pw8 --lr 1.2e-3 --stack-loop 2,8,2 --pulse-budget 507000 --pool-lifts-ceiling --granule-power 8, on v18c; the parameters of fs-loop6-lift-pw8

base: fs-loop6-lift-pw8 (1.287005): the lifted loop with power-law cells at 6e-4 of full_size_power_cells.json, the same seed and measure. Beside it: fs-loop6-lift (1.300729), fs-loop12-lift (1.297606) and the rate pilot's Transformer at 6e-4 and 1.2e-3 (1.28370, 1.27625).
runs: 24,000 updates of 8 windows of 512 bytes, warmup 1,000, cosine over the run, seed 20001, as the base. Queued on GPU 1 with an AFTER line on fsp-lift at priority 33, behind pool_gradient's jobs (priorities 30 to 32); GPU_MEM 40, under MPS as full.sh pilots are. A run that the close stops goes on in the next window.
measure: full.sh's score, as for the base: averaged weights on the first 2,000,000 validation bytes as 16 unbroken streams after 8,192 lead bytes, bits of every piece kept; paired with fs-loop6-lift-pw8 (experiments/compare_stream_scores.py) and split by context (experiments/gap_by_piece.py, near 240, far 8,192); the pulses a byte; the parameters.
reading: Each arm is read alone against fs-loop6-lift-pw8. An arm at least 0.005 better with the paired interval clear of zero joins the next full-length run (skip fibres as --stack-skips level; the rate as 1.2e-3). Between 0 and 0.005 better with the interval clear of zero: reported as unclear, and the change stays out unless a second seed brings the mean of the two to 0.005. Otherwise it stays out. If both arms pass, the next full-length run carries both only after a pilot with both (a record of its own), since their gains need not add. Pulses a byte are reported beside; if an arm's are more than a tenth above the base's, every claim states them.
seen_before_recording: skip_fibres_with_data.json with all its results; full_size_loop_variants.json with result_rate; full_size_power_cells.json with its result; power_cells_in_loop_screen.json with its result. No full-size run with skip fibres and none with power-law cells at 1.2e-3 has trained.

Power-law cells gain 0.0137 over plain cells at 6e-4 and cost 0.0022 at 1.2e-3.

result_rate.reading: The rate stays out: at 1.2e-3 the lifted loop with power-law cells is 0.0128 worse than at 6e-4, with the paired interval clear of zero on the wrong side, so the next full-length run keeps 6e-4, the rate fsp-lift2 is training at. The loss is on new contexts (0.019 over 76% of the bytes) and far copies (0.037); where the eight bytes before a byte ran earlier with another follower the faster rate is 0.093 better, over 5% of the bytes, and near copies do not differ. Pulses a byte are 0.5% above the base's (517,743 against 515,340), far under the tenth that would have to be stated. One seed.
result_rate.seen while reading: The expectation in this record's why, that power-law cells' best rate may differ from plain cells' because they learn faster early, holds in the other direction from the one that would have helped: their best rate is not above 6e-4, and the gain of the cells is tied to the rate. No rate under 6e-4 has been tried with them at full size.
